A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SASHA framework and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The duplicated appendix in v1 was matched against the single expanded appendix in v3; its consolidation does not represent removal of scientific evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original SASHA experiments on CAMELYON16 and TCGA-NSCLC, including classification results, ablations, timing, calibration and patch-selection analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds multiclass evaluations, Zoom-MIL comparisons, a CONCH ablation and computational profiling.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Section 3.4 and Appendix A.2.3 generalize the reported reward from negative binary cross-entropy to cross-entropy, accompanying the multiclass extension. The HAFED architecture, targeted state updates, PPO training and deterministic inference procedure otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the two retained binary tasks, v3 evaluates four-class metastasis classification on Camelyon+ and three-class benign/atypical/malignant classification on grouped BRACS labels. This substantially broadens the represented data and diagnostic task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Zoom-MIL at k=80, 160 and 300 to both existing benchmark comparisons. The previous full-resolution comparators and RLogist remain; the multiclass comparison extends the already evaluated ACMIL and DTFD methods.

E3.justification: v3 introduces minority-class oversampling and weighted multiclass metrics, plus fixed Zoom-MIL sampling budgets. Budget equivalence is only approximate: its justification uses about 800 patches, while Appendix A.1 reports about 212 for TCGA-NSCLC. Table 13 also explicitly excludes patch preprocessing from total time, whereas v1 described inclusive timing; v3 retains conflicting inclusive prose. Existing binary splits and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a CONCH encoder ablation testing dependence on the original feature extractor. Table 13 adds component-level runtime analysis. Existing attention, state-update, random-policy, reward-schedule, stochastic-inference and tumor-localization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean and standard-deviation reporting, the five-split by three-seed protocol for limited-budget comparisons, shaded standard deviations for agent trajectories and patch-selection significance reporting. Added result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice or establish increased run counts.

E6.justification: Existing binary classification and control scores are retained, but v3 adds Zoom-MIL, CONCH and multiclass results. Table 9 reports SASHA-0.2 accuracies of 0.871±0.005 on Camelyon+ and 0.598±0.016 on BRACS. Table 13 adds component timings and totals of 15.50/27.49 seconds for SASHA-0.1/0.2 under its stated overhead exclusion. Appendix A.6 also revises the reported HAFED component count from 330K to 300K.

T1.justification: The hit-ratio and compressibility definitions are retained, with no new theoretical assumptions, proofs or derivations. v3 replaces the standard ECE formulas with shorter prose; this reduces explanatory detail rather than introducing a substantive theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: selective sampling achieves competitive diagnosis with lower computational and representation costs, supported by HAFED, TSU and reinforcement learning. The additional experiments do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 identifies TSU similarity computation as a secondary runtime bottleneck and describes SASHA-0.2 calibration as intermediate rather than comparable to HAFED. Appendix A.6 adds a proposed joint-training extension with stability caveats and discusses domain shift as a boundary on clinical applicability.

D1.justification: v3 adds a SASHA implementation-repository pointer, class counts and processing details for the added datasets, oversampling information, Zoom-MIL configurations and timing-component definitions. Existing architecture, optimizer, training-duration and hardware disclosures are largely retained; the HAFED parameter-count correction does not establish an architectural change.

R1.justification: Four cited works are added for BRACS, Camelyon+, CONCH and Zoom-MIL. Related work now contrasts Zoom-MIL's fixed top-k selection with adaptive contextual sampling, while retaining the existing MIL and reinforcement-learning positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most methodological prose remain, with localized rewriting in the introduction, methods and Appendices A.4–A.6. v3 consolidates the duplicated appendix after the references, corrects internal references, shortens the ECE explanation and adds acknowledgements and conference information.

P2.justification: The table presentation expands substantially: Tables 1–2 gain comparison and ablation rows, and four new tables present dataset splits, multiclass performance and runtime decomposition. All five unique figure images are unchanged, but duplicate appendix displays are removed and several retained tables and figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through multiclass evaluations, a non-RL sampling comparator and a modern encoder ablation while retaining the original results. The implementation pointer, runtime breakdown and appendix consolidation improve usability. These gains are limited by incompletely justified Zoom-MIL budget matching, inconsistent timing accounting and a less precise ECE description, supporting a modest overall improvement.
